comparison.text: Official Indian AQI: 303 out of 500, category 'Very Poor'. That is the government's own scale.
comparison.source_name: CPCB, National Air Quality Index (PM2.5 breakpoints)
comparison.caveat: Computed from PM2.5 alone. The full CPCB AQI takes the worst sub-index across pollutants, so the official city AQI can be higher on days another pollutant dominates.

comparison.text: Today's air is worse than 84 percent of days this season in Mumbai. Ranked, logged, versioned.
comparison.caveat: Season means the trailing 90 days of this project's own observations. Small archive early on means noisy percentiles, and the repo shows exactly how small.

comparison.text: Today's air is worse than 100 percent of days this season in Pune. Ranked, logged, versioned.
comparison.caveat: Season means the trailing 90 days of this project's own observations. Small archive early on means noisy percentiles, and the repo shows exactly how small.

comparison.text: Breathing Bengaluru air today = smoking 1.2 cigarettes. No lighter needed.
comparison.source_name: Berkeley Earth, Air Pollution and Cigarette Equivalence (Richard A. Muller and Elizabeth A. Muller)
comparison.caveat: A rule of thumb comparing health effects, not identical smoke. The authors call it a rough estimate, and unlike smoking, polluted air is breathed by everyone including kids.

comparison.text: A week of air like this = 8 cigarettes. Your lungs are keeping the receipts.
comparison.source_name: Berkeley Earth, Air Pollution and Cigarette Equivalence
comparison.caveat: Extends the Berkeley Earth per-day rule of thumb across a week at the same level. Real weeks vary day to day.
